content: Cefpodoxime is a cephalosporin antibiotic prescribed to treat bacterial infections, including pneumonia, bronchitis, gonorrhea, and infections of the ear, skin, throat, and urinary tract. It is not effective against colds, flu, or other viral infections. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Cefpodoxime is available as a tablet or liquid to be taken orally. It is typically taken every 12 hours (twice daily) for 7 to 14 days. A single dose is used to treat gonorrhea. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take cefpodoxime exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. Shake the liquid form well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. Continue taking cefpodoxime even if you feel better, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking cefpodoxime, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cefadroxil or cephalexin), penicillin, or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antibiotics, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), probenecid, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have had kidney or liver disease, colitis, or stomach problems. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking cefpodoxime, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking cefpodoxime. Take cefpodoxime tablets with food. The liquid form can be taken with or without food. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Cefpodoxime may cause side effects. Minor side effects include upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, and mild skin rash. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, unusual bleeding or bruising, sore throat, and vaginal infections. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store cefpodoxime in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Tablets should be stored at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Discard any outdated or unused medication. Liquid cefpodoxime should be refrigerated, tightly closed, and discarded after 14 days. Do not freeze it. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal of unused medication. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order lab tests to monitor your response to cefpodoxime. If you have diabetes, consult your doctor before changing your diet or medication dosage. Use Clinistix or TesTape (not Clinitest) to test your urine for sugar while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing cefpodoxime, contact your doctor.
